info.description: REST API for the Nicoflow GTD task-management platform. Covers authentication & user management, Areas, Projects, Tasks (CRUD, quick actions, filter/sort/search), Subtasks, Focus and Time-Spread.
info.title: Nicoflow API

get.description: Lists the user's areas, cursor-paginated, with optional name search.

post.description: Creates an area. Free plan allows up to 3 areas.

patch.description: Bulk-updates area displayOrder in one transaction (atomic; a foreign id rolls the whole batch back).

404.description: AREA_NOT_FOUND (a foreign id — whole batch rolled back)

get.description: Returns every area with its projects nested — the payload the board renders from.
Lists the projects within one area, cursor-paginated, with optional filters.

post.description: Creates a project inside an area. Free plan allows up to 5 projects total.

get.description: Retrieves a single area by ID. Cross-user access returns 404.

delete.description: Deletes an area; its projects are cascade-deleted (their tasks survive unfiled).

patch.description: Partial update of an area (name, color, icon).

post.description: Changes the authenticated user's password. Re-verifies currentPassword via bcrypt, enforces the register password policy on newPassword, revokes all refresh tokens, and issues a fresh token pair to the caller (every other device is signed out; the caller stays signed in). Sets a new HttpOnly refresh cookie.

200.description: New access token + rotated refresh cookie

401.description: UNAUTHORIZED (missing access token or wrong current password)

post.description: Sends a password-reset email. Always returns 200 regardless of whether the email exists (no user enumeration).

Authenticates by email or username and returns a JWT access token plus an HttpOnly refresh cookie. When REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION is enabled, an unverified account is rejected with 403 EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED after the password check (so verification state is never leaked to a wrong password).

200.description: Access token + user; Set-Cookie refresh token

401.description: UNAUTHORIZED (invalid credentials; identical for unknown user and wrong password)

post.description: Revokes the single refresh token carried by the cookie and clears it. Authenticates off the HttpOnly refresh cookie, not the access token. Idempotent — a missing or already-deleted token still returns 204.
Revokes every refresh token for the authenticated user. Requires a valid access token (revokes by the userID claim).

204.description: All sessions revoked; refresh cookie cleared

post.description: Rotates the refresh token (delete-old/insert-new) and issues a fresh access token. The raw refresh token is read from the HttpOnly cookie (preferred) or a JSON body. Replaying a consumed token is reuse and revokes all of the user's sessions.

200.description: New access token + rotated refresh cookie

post.description: Creates a user and sends a verification email. Does not log the user in — no token is issued and no cookie is set; the user must verify (when enforced) then log in.
Re-sends the email-verification link. Always returns 200 (no user enumeration).
Sets a new password using the single-use reset token from the email. Revokes all active refresh tokens on success.
Confirms a user's email using the single-use token from the verification email.

get.description: Lists the caller's bucket items, newest first. Processed and unprocessed items are both returned; the client partitions them into Inbox / Archived.

post.description: Quick-captures a thought into the bucket. Content is 1–500 characters (trimmed).

get.description: Retrieves a single bucket item by ID. Cross-user access returns 404 (no existence leak).

delete.description: Hard-deletes a bucket item regardless of processed state.

patch.description: Edits the content of an unprocessed bucket item. Editing a processed item returns 409.

post.description: Converts an unprocessed item into a task (requires projectId + taskDetails) or note (requires projectId + noteDetails), or trashes it. taskDetails.scheduledTime and taskDetails.recurrence give the task path full parity with plain task creation — when recurrence is set, a recurrence rule is created (materializing instance #1) instead of a plain task. Already-processed items return 409.

get.description: Read-only overlay of the user's selected Google calendars for an inclusive date range (max 62 days). Never returns 5xx for a Google-side failure — the response carries `googleStatus` (`ok`|`disconnected`|`error`) with an empty list instead, so a Google outage cannot break the calendar view. `refresh=true` bypasses the short server-side cache.

parameters.description: Bypass the cache and re-query Google
parameters.name: refresh

422.description: INVALID_INPUT (missing bound, bad date, or span > 62 days)

get.description: The calendars the user can read, each flagged with whether it currently overlays the Nicoflow calendar. A connection with no stored selection reports the primary calendar as selected, matching the overlay's default.

put.description: Replaces the overlay selection. Capped at 5 calendars — each selected calendar is a separate Google API call per ranged fetch. Duplicates are collapsed rather than rejected. Returns the full calendar list with the new selection applied.

422.description: INVALID_INPUT — missing field, empty ID, or more than 5 calendars

get.description: Returns a deterministically-ranked short list of the user's active tasks (across all projects) that fit the given time/energy. Scoring: energy match, time-budget fit (over-budget excluded), due/overdue escalation, scheduled proximity, priority tiebreak.
get.summary: Focus — what can I do right now?

get.description: Returns the caller's habits, newest first, each with a short heatmap window (14 cells) alongside its derived counters — enough for a board to draw a ribbon per card without a follow-up request. Archived habits are excluded unless includeArchived=true. Free users may hold 3 active habits; a downgraded user keeps every habit visible and checkable, only creation is blocked.

post.description: Creates a habit. scheduleKind is one of daily, weekdays (requires byWeekday) or weekly_quota (requires timesPerWeek). polarity is build or quit and is immutable afterwards. Free plan allows 3 active habits.

get.description: The canonical subject list. Subjects are cosmetic — they drive the card icon and never scheduling or targets. labelKey is an i18n key, not a display string. A client meeting an unknown slug renders a fallback icon rather than failing, so the catalog can gain entries without a client release.

Returns the habits still owed right now, for the Today-page strip. A weekdays habit appears only on its own days; a weekly-quota habit appears every day until its week's quota is met, then goes quiet. Archived and already-completed habits are excluded.

Retrieves a single habit with its derived counters and the heatmap window behind them. Cells are day cells for daily/weekdays habits and week cells (carrying quota progress) for weekly_quota habits — the granularity streakUnit announces. Cross-user access returns 404, never 403.

delete.description: Archives a habit by default: the row is retired, the check-in history is retained — it is the user's record of what they did — and a plan slot is freed. Pass permanent=true to delete it outright instead, which cascades to every check-in and cannot be undone. The default is the reversible one on purpose. Cross-user access returns 404, never 403.

parameters.description: Destroy the habit and its history instead of archiving it
parameters.name: permanent

patch.description: Edits a habit. polarity is immutable — sending it returns 422. Changing the schedule applies forward only; periods already scored keep their shape. Set archived to true to retire a habit (freeing a plan slot) or false to restore it.

post.description: Records one dated entry. Omit date to check in for today — the server resolves it from the user's timezone and never accepts a client-supplied "today". Omit value to use the habit's target. Idempotent per (habit, date): a repeat call updates the value. A past date is a backfill and must fall inside the window (7 days for daily/weekdays habits, the current and previous week for weekly quota); future dates are refused.

422.description: INVALID_INPUT (future date, outside the backfill window, negative value, or archived habit)

delete.description: Removes one dated entry, reverting the day to not-done. Omit date to undo today. Idempotent: undoing a date with no entry succeeds, because the day is already not done.

422.description: INVALID_INPUT (future date, outside the backfill window, or archived habit)

get.description: Returns the project's notes ordered by updated_at DESC. Each item carries a 200-char excerpt and NO content — never render a note body from this response. Notes are Free and unlimited.

post.description: Files a new note under a project. content is optional (defaults to an empty document). content_text is always server-derived — a client-sent value is rejected. Notes are Free and unlimited; this endpoint never returns PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Bodies over 1 MB are refused.

422.description: INVALID_INPUT (bad title/content/projectId, or body over 1 MB)

get.description: Returns up to 10 title matches for the @-mention autocomplete, row-isolated to the requesting user. excludeId omits the note currently being edited (a note cannot usefully mention itself). Notes are Free and unlimited; this endpoint never returns PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

parameters.description: Note id to omit from results (the note being edited)
parameters.name: excludeId

get.description: Retrieves a single note including its full document. Cross-user access returns 404, never 403.

delete.description: Hard-deletes a note. Cross-user access returns 404, never 403.

patch.description: Partial update guarded by optimistic concurrency. version is REQUIRED and must match the stored row; a stale version returns 409 and writes nothing. On 409 a client must surface a conflict state and stop autosaving — never retry silently. A successful save increments version.

parameters.description: Fields to change plus the version last read
parameters.name: request

200.description: The updated note at its new version

409.description: CONFLICT (stale version — the note moved on)

422.description: INVALID_INPUT (missing version, bad title/content, or body over 1 MB)

get.description: Returns the list-shape view (no content) of every note that mentions the given note. Empty array, not null, when there are no backlinks. Cross-user access returns 404, never 403.

200.description: Notes that link to this one

get.description: Lists the user's notifications, cursor-paginated, newest first, with an optional read filter.

Returns the user's notification preferences. An absent row yields the defaults ({ emailDigest:true, pushEnabled:false, smsEnabled:false, morningDigestEnabled:true, eveningDigestEnabled:true, streaksEnabled:true }). Push/SMS toggles are stored but inert until E-037.

put.description: Partially or fully updates the user's notification preferences (lazy upsert). morningHour must be 5–11, eveningHour 18–22. Push/SMS toggles persist but have no delivery path until E-037.

400.description: INVALID_INPUT (bad body or hour out of range)

post.description: Stores a browser Web Push subscription for the user (Pro-only). Upserts on endpoint. Free-plan callers get PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

delete.description: Removes the user's Web Push subscription for the given endpoint. Idempotent.

patch.description: Marks every unread notification read and returns how many were updated.

get.description: Returns the number of unread notifications — the cheap poll target for the bell badge.

delete.description: Hard-deletes a notification. Cross-user access returns 404.

patch.description: Marks a single notification read. Cross-user access returns 404.

get.description: Lists the user's projects across all areas, cursor-paginated, with optional filters.

patch.description: Bulk-updates project displayOrder in one transaction (atomic; a foreign id rolls the whole batch back).

404.description: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND (a foreign id — whole batch rolled back)

get.description: Retrieves a single project by ID. Cross-user access returns 404.

delete.description: Deletes a project; its tasks are cascade-deleted.

patch.description: Partial update of a project. Setting areaId moves the project between areas (null detaches).

get.description: Lists the tasks within a project, with optional filtering, sorting and case-insensitive ILIKE search over title+notes.

post.description: Creates a task in a project. Title-only is valid (quick-add); other fields default server-side (status=active, priority=medium, energy=medium, rollsOver=true). Free plan allows 50 active tasks per project.

parameters.description: Task to create (only title is required)
parameters.name: body

get.description: Searches the user's tasks, projects and areas via PostgreSQL full-text (plainto_tsquery), ranked by relevance.

Flat list of the user's tasks scheduled within an inclusive date range, ordered by (scheduledFor, scheduledTime NULLS FIRST, displayOrder). Unlike Time Spread no roll-forward is applied — a task is returned on the date it is actually scheduled for. Both bounds are required and the span is capped at 62 days.
get.summary: List tasks in a date range (calendar)

422.description: INVALID_INPUT (missing bound, bad date, or span > 62 days)

get.description: Retrieves a single task by ID. Cross-user access returns 404 (no existence leak).

delete.description: Hard-deletes a task; its subtasks cascade.

patch.description: Partial update of any mutable field. status→done sets completedAt server-side; moving away from done clears it. A PATCH that moves a task into active is subject to the plan limit.

Reaps one recurring occurrence to (cancelled, missed) — the same terminal state the overdue sweep sets automatically once its due date passes, just triggered now instead of at the next local midnight. Only eligible for a still-active recurring occurrence due today or earlier.
patch.summary: Manually mark a recurring occurrence missed

422.description: TASK_NOT_MISSABLE — not recurring, not active, already reaped, or its occurrence date is still in the future

patch.description: Moves a task to a target displayOrder; siblings in the project are repacked to a contiguous 0..n-1 sequence (transactional).
Sets the soft scheduledFor intention, optional scheduledTime (HH:MM, Pro-only) and rollsOver flag. scheduledFor null (or absent) unschedules. A bad date returns 400 INVALID_DATE.

parameters.description: scheduledFor (ISO date or null) + optional scheduledTime + rollsOver
parameters.name: body

post.description: Marks the live recurring occurrence skipped — the user deliberately opting out, without breaking their streak. Unlike mark-missed, eligible any time (including ahead of the occurrence's due date). Best-effort cancels any pending notification tied to the task.

409.description: TASK_NOT_SKIPPABLE — not recurring, not the live instance, or not active

patch.description: Status-only update (checkbox toggle, cancel). Same completedAt side-effects and plan-limit semantics as the full PATCH.

get.description: Lists a task's subtasks, ordered by position. Parent-task ownership is enforced.

post.description: Creates a subtask under a task. Appends to the end unless position is given.

delete.description: Deletes a subtask. Parent-task ownership enforced.

patch.description: Partial update of a subtask (title, done, position). Parent-task ownership enforced.

get.description: Buckets the user's active tasks into today/tomorrow/thisWeek with the no-guilt roll-forward (a past soft-scheduled task with rollsOver=true carries to today instead of going overdue). done/cancelled are excluded.

parameters.description: IANA timezone for day bucketing (e.g. Asia/Jerusalem); defaults to UTC
parameters.name: tz

delete.description: Soft-deletes the authenticated user (sets deleted_at) and revokes all refresh tokens.

patch.description: Updates profile fields. All fields are optional; omitted fields are left unchanged.

get.description: Returns the authenticated user's profile.

weekStart.description:
Calendar preferences are individually optional too, so a client changing
only the day window never has to echo back a week_start it did not read.

calendar.description:
Calendar always travels with the user: the grid needs it on first paint,
and a second round trip would render one frame of the wrong week.

progress.description: Set only on week cells, where a period accumulates toward a quota.

cells.description:
Cells is the heatmap window. A list read carries ListRibbonDays of it and
a scalar read RibbonDays — same field, different width, so a board and a
detail page render the same component against the same shape.

Optional rather than required: it is omitted wherever there is no window
to show, and a client that predates it simply renders no ribbon instead of
breaking. Same contract style as periodProgress.

loggedToday.description:
LoggedToday is whether an entry exists for today — NOT whether the period
is satisfied. The two diverge on a quota habit: at 1 of 3 the week is
unmet (CompletedToday false) but today is logged, and a control that
keys off CompletedToday would check in again rather than undo.

periodProgress.description:
PeriodProgress is the quota habit's "2 of 3 this week". Null for day
habits — the client must not read a missing value as 0/0.

streakUnit.description:
StreakUnit tells the client which noun to print ("12 days" vs "5 weeks")
and which heatmap granularity to draw. Normalising everything to weeks was
rejected: it would show "0 weeks" to someone on a 6-day run, which kills
the daily feedback the feature is built on.

subtaskCount.description: SubtaskCount / OpenSubtaskCount are always populated, on every read.

totalFocusSeconds.description:
TotalFocusSeconds is the SUM of the task's closed focus segments (E-049).
Enriched only on Focus + GetTask; 0 on the project task-list, where a
per-row SUM would be pure cost for a value the list never renders.
